input.question: Which award did Hideo Kojima receive?

documents.text: As the sun set over the Stockholm skyline, Hideo Kojima stepped out of the sleek, black town car and onto the cobblestone streets of the Old Town. The air was crisp, carrying the whispers of centuries past, and the legendary game designer felt an inexplicable sense of belonging. He had been summoned to this enigmatic city for a purpose, one that only a select few knew. Kojima's eyes scanned the façade of the Grand Hôtel, its elegant architecture a testament to the country's rich history. He was greeted by a dignified figure, resplendent in a tailcoat, who introduced himself as Count Carl Gustaf von Rosen, Chancellor of the Order of the Sword. "Mr. Kojima, it is an honor to finally meet you," the Count said, his voice like polished silver. "Your contributions to the world of gaming have not gone unnoticed. You have been chosen to receive a prestigious award, one that recognizes your unwavering dedication to the pursuit of excellence." As they entered the hotel's opulent ballroom, Kojima's gaze wandered across the assembly of dignitaries, their faces a blur of curiosity and admiration. He spotted a few familiar faces, fellow visionaries who had pushed the boundaries of their respective crafts. The atmosphere was alive with anticipation, the soft hum of conversation punctuated by the clinking of crystal glasses. Count von Rosen led Kojima to a velvet-draped podium, where a solitary, ornate box awaited. The Chancellor's hands moved with deliberate precision as he opened the box, revealing a gleaming, golden sword. The room fell silent, the only sound the soft rustle of the sword's silk-lined scabbard. "Hideo Kojima, in recognition of your innovative spirit and your unwavering commitment to the art of storytelling, we hereby confer upon you the title of Knight of the Order of the Sword," the Count declared, his voice resonating through the hallowed hall. As Kojima accepted the sword, its weight settling comfortably in his hand, he felt an unspoken connection to the centuries-old tradition of chivalry. It was a symbol of his own unyielding pursuit of excellence, a reminder that the boundaries of reality were meant to be pushed, and that the art of storytelling knew no borders.

accepted_answers: Knight of the Order of the Sword
